PullRequest.Title: chat: add customization migration assessment telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Customization migration assessment telemetry with explicit lifecycle-owned reporting.

- keep computation and hint generation free of telemetry side effects
- expose an explicit `reportMigrationTelemetry(...)` method with aggregate-only payloads
- report completed assessments from the four intended lifecycle surfaces:
  - new chat in the editor
  - new-session composer in the Agents Window
  - existing session open
  - persisted session restore
- emit one event per non-empty migration category with only trigger, category, warning severity, and count
- remove informational severity until it has distinct product semantics
- deduplicate session-open assessments across child-chat navigation while preserving genuine session entry and side-open reporting
- bound lifecycle assessment concurrency to two during multi-session restore
- add lifecycle-owner tests for all four reporting surfaces

Refs #332990

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- targeted ESLint for changed lifecycle files
- focused Chromium browser tests: 143 passing, 2 pending
  - `ChatEditor` editor new-chat lifecycle
  - `NewChatWidget` Agents new-session lifecycle
  - `SessionsService` session-open, child-chat deduplication, side-open, and bounded restore lifecycles
  - `CustomizationMigrationService` aggregate payload and telemetry-free compute/hint behavior
- `git diff --check`
- `npm run valid-layers-check` completed the structural layer check; its type-check phase is locally blocked by unrelated current-tree Copilot SDK type mismatches under `src/vs/platform/agentHost`

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call flow is explicit: restore schedules one task per resolved session; explicit navigation calls `_cancelRestore`; `Limiter` retains outstanding factories until consumed; and the changed callback omits the token even though the helper supports it. The assessment's file discovery, source-folder scans, and MCP support resolution are directly visible in `CustomizationMigrationService`. Exact milliseconds vary with customization and MCP counts, but cancellation failure and scaling are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Queued filesystem/extension-provider discovery, customization scans, and per-root MCP support assessment work.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Wasted work grows with the number of persisted visible sessions still running or queued at cancellation, and within each assessment with customization-file candidates and configured MCP servers; the limiter caps concurrency at two but does not reduce total stale work.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive stale I/O and CPU contention after navigation cancels startup restore.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, restoring or abandoning persisted sessions performed no migration telemetry assessments, so cancellation left no assessment queue to drain.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Startup restore now queues a full customization migration assessment for every restored session. Although each enqueue receives the restore cancellation token, queued and running factories discard it once admitted by the limiter.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The diff adds one `_reportCustomizationMigrationTelemetry(..., token)` enqueue for every session restored at RIGHT lines 1590 and 1638, but the newly added limiter callback at RIGHT line 939 invokes `reportCustomizationMigrationTelemetry` without that token, so it uses `CancellationToken.None`.
Findings.Title: Cancel queued migration assessments when restore is abandoned
Findings.Impact: If the user opens a session while startup is restoring several persisted sessions—especially while agent/customization state is cold—all stale restore assessments continue in the background. They consume filesystem/extension-provider I/O and MCP assessment CPU after the restore was abandoned, contending with the newly opened session and prolonging post-navigation activity.
Findings.Evidence: `_cancelRestore()` cancels the restore token specifically so explicit opens bail out of cold restore work. `_reportCustomizationMigrationTelemetry` checks that token only before `Limiter.queue`; once queued, line 939 calls the helper without it. `Limiter` does not inspect cancellation and drains all outstanding factories. Each factory calls `computeMigrations`, which lists prompt files for multiple types, queries source folders for candidate types, and creates a per-working-directory MCP support scope that resolves all MCP servers/configuration. Therefore cancellation while two tasks run leaves both running and every queued session assessment still starts afterward.
Findings.Recommendation: Recheck the restore token inside the limiter factory and pass it to `reportCustomizationMigrationTelemetry`; make the MCP assessment wait cancellation-aware as well so already-running work releases its scope promptly. This preserves the concurrency limit and telemetry for restores that remain active while dropping only superseded work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents Window startup restores persisted visible sessions, then the user explicitly opens another session before restore telemetry drains.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session-resource redirection and resolving the active persisted session are on the startup restore critical path. The new telemetry assessments are fire-and-forget after sessions are placed, so they are off the direct restore critical path, but they continue to contend with foreground work after an explicit open cancels restore.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve persisted session resources, potentially waiting on a cold agent host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resource-resolution call per persisted visible slot, concurrently, bounded by the existing 10-second aggregate race.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-slot resolution already occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This must finish or time out before initial grid layout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover prompt/customization files and evaluate migration candidates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full assessment per successfully restored session; cold prompt discovery is effectively one call per prompt type through shared promises, while source-folder filtering is per session/category and MCP assessment is per distinct working-directory scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Scheduled off-path after placement, but consumes resources during startup and continues after cancellation because the token is dropped in the limiter callback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve MCP support, including configuration-variable resolution and waiting for initial local MCP inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to two assessments concurrently; one MCP support scope per distinct session type/root key among active assessments, evaluating all configured and installed MCP servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Restore did not acquire MCP assessment scopes for telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the direct layout path, but can overlap and contend with a foreground session open.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Persisted visible-session count after deduplication; customization-file candidate count; configured/installed MCP-server count; distinct session working-directory scopes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Persisted resources are redirected with `Promise.all`; late sessions wait concurrently. Migration assessments are globally limited to two, but every restored session is queued and the limiter is not cancellation-aware.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt-file discovery is cached and coalesced per prompt type once the locator events are initialized, so cold restore generally pays one discovery per type rather than per session. Source-folder filtering and MCP support are session/root dependent; concurrent sessions with the same MCP root key share only while their refcounted scopes overlap, and completed one-shot scopes are disposed rather than retained. There is no negative/result cache for the aggregate migration assessment.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: per-session scheduling, limiter cardinality, token cancellation, and the dropped token are directly established by the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of visible restored sessions and configured customizations/MCP servers varies, as does filesystem/provider latency. The stale queue after cancellation is deterministic; only its wall-clock cost varies.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the diff introduces per-session assessment work and fails to cancel queued/running work when the owning restore is abandoned.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an existing Agents session, navigate among its child chats, switch sessions, or open a session to the side.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session resolution/loading remains on the open critical path. Telemetry starts after load for async opens, or immediately after synchronous showing, and is fire-and-forget; it does not block the open promise.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve and load the selected session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session-resource resolution and session load per explicit open, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same open/load calls existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the session is usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute migration categories and report up to four aggregate events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One assessment per genuine active-session entry, deduplicated across child-chat navigation; warm file discovery is shared, while session/root-specific source and MCP checks remain.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening a session did not compute migration telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget, but shares the limiter and underlying resources with restore assessments.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of genuine session entries, customization candidates, and MCP servers/root scopes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Assessments share the same global limiter with restore and run at most two concurrently. A foreground open assessment can queue behind stale restore assessments.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt file lists are shared/cached by type. There is no aggregate assessment cache keyed by session or customization generation. The active-session boolean suppresses child-chat navigation within one entry but resets after switching to another session, so a later genuine re-entry reassesses.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the invocation and deduplication behavior; moderate for material impact during ordinary, non-cancelled opens because it is off-path and caches reduce file discovery.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frequent alternation between sessions can repeat assessment work, but typical entry frequency and underlying cache warmth are uncertain; no separate high-confidence user-visible regression beyond the cancellation issue was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: child-chat duplication is explicitly suppressed and ordinary assessment work is bounded/off-path; contention caused by stale restore tasks is covered by the reported issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or replace a new-session draft in the Agents Window through workspace selection, session-type selection, quick chat, or late provider registration.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Draft creation is on the composer setup path; the telemetry assessment is launched by an autorun and is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover customization files, inspect session source folders, and assess MCP support for the draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One assessment each time the active uncreated draft object/resource changes; usually one, with additional calls after workspace/session-type changes or provider-driven recreation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Draft changes did not run migration assessments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the direct composer critical path but overlaps user interaction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of draft replacements before prior assessments settle, plus customization/MCP counts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No composer-local limiter or coalescer is added. Provider-driven draft recreation cancels session creation but does not cancel already launched telemetry assessment work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt discovery is shared by type, but aggregate results are not cached by draft resource. A replacement draft receives a new assessment even if it supersedes a still-running draft.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for uncancelled per-draft invocation; lower for material user-visible cost at typical cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Automatic provider churn and rapid user reselection can overlap work, but realistic cardinality is usually small and no direct latency symptom is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: uncancelled overlap is possible, but expected multiplicity is too low/uncertain to establish a separate actionable regression at review confidence.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a new chat in an editor and bind an empty agent-host session model.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Editor model resolution is awaited; migration telemetry starts only after the empty model is bound and is fire-and-forget. The editor operation token is passed to the helper, so superseded file/source work can observe cancellation, though MCP assessment currently has limited cancellation propagation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the chat editor input and session model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing model/session resolution per editor input, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same model resolution existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before editor content binds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover customization candidates and assess MCP support before aggregate telemetry reporting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full migration assessment for each resolved empty contributed-chat input with a session resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Binding an empty editor model did not run this assessment.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct empty new-chat editor inputs/groups and customization/MCP counts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No editor-specific limiter; normal editor pane operation cancellation supersedes prior `setInput` calls. Typical cardinality is one assessment per distinct empty new-chat editor input.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt discovery is shared by type and the aggregate assessment itself is not cached. Distinct editor inputs each assess independently; reopening the same matching input normally avoids `setInput` unless forced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the new call path and boundaries; moderate for meaningful impact because it is post-bind and normally one-shot.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Forced reloads and multiple empty editor groups can multiply work, but normal pane matching and cancellation keep expected cardinality low.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the added work is off the editor bind critical path, tokenized, and expected to run once per distinct new editor input.

Scenarios.Scenario: Serialize and emit aggregate migration-assessment telemetry.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `publicLog2` calls happen synchronously after assessment completion but are on fire-and-forget lifecycle tasks rather than UI critical paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and enqueue aggregate trigger/category/severity/count telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero to four aggregate telemetry calls per assessment, one per non-empty category.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No migration assessment telemetry was emitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off direct UI progress paths; telemetry transport is handled by the existing telemetry service.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed maximum of four categories per completed assessment.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most four event calls per completed assessment; Sessions assessments inherit the global limit of two, while editor/composer calls may overlap independently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Reporting consumes the computed migration array and retains no cache or long-lived payload. Empty categories emit nothing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the loop has four migration categories and emits only non-empty aggregate payloads.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Transport batching details are outside the changed code, but payload count and size are statically bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: payload size and per-assessment event fan-out are tightly bounded; the material cost is the assessment computation, not serialization.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 11 changed files and traced the new assessment through Agents restore/open/new-session and editor-new-chat lifecycles. One performance regression was submitted: restore cancellation is lost inside the limiter, causing all stale queued assessments to drain. Normal telemetry serialization is bounded, and other lifecycle work is off-path or low-cardinality enough not to support additional findings.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
